which has reported healthy

The embedded resolver handles a query for `<service>` as it handles a name that it
does not have a record for. For a service none of whose containers has reported healthy since
the service was created, this holds from when the service is created, without a ceiling.

<a id="SWARM-SD-SERVICE-NAME-UPSTREAM"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SD-SERVICE-NAME-UPSTREAM**: A vip service's name without a running or healthy task goes upstream

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-REPLICAS](#SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-REPLICAS), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-TASKS](#SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-TASKS), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NONE-HEALTHY](#SWARM-SD-VIP-NONE-HEALTHY) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-SD-VIP](#SWARM-SD-VIP), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-REPLICAS](#SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-REPLICAS), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-TASKS](#SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-TASKS), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NONE-HEALTHY](#SWARM-SD-VIP-NONE-HEALTHY) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-SD-SERVICE-NAMES](#REQ-SWARM-SD-SERVICE-NAMES)

When a service in the `vip` endpoint mode has no running container, was created with no
replicas, or has no container that has reported healthy, the embedded resolver forwards an A
query for the service's name to the upstream servers, as it does for a name that it does not
have a record for, and returns their answer ([moby/moby#52049](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/52049)).

<a id="SWARM-SD-VIP-UNREACHABLE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SD-VIP-UNREACHABLE**: The VIP of a service without running tasks gives EHOSTUNREACH

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Rationale:* How a connection to a VIP without backends fails follows from the load balancer's implementation ([RAT-SWARM-EMPTY-VIP-FAILURE-MODE](#RAT-SWARM-EMPTY-VIP-FAILURE-MODE))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes, and a service in vip mode that still exists, such as one scaled to 0
replicas

Once no container of the service is running, a TCP connection to the service's VIP fails at the
client with `EHOSTUNREACH`. The client does not get a TCP reset.

<a id="SWARM-SD-RENAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SD-RENAME**: A renamed standalone container resolves by its new name on other nodes

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](container-dns.md#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC), [REQ-SWARM-SD-CONTAINER-NAME](#REQ-SWARM-SD-CONTAINER-NAME) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A standalone container on an attachable overlay, whose hostname and network
aliases differ from its name in more than the case of their letters

Once `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container, with a new name that differs from
its old name in more than the case of its letters, responds 204, its new name resolves for
containers on other nodes within the [*reassignment ceiling (300 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT). Within the same ceiling, its old name stops resolving to its address
for those containers.

<a id="SWARM-SD-ALIAS-ROLLING-UPDATE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SD-ALIAS-ROLLING-UPDATE**: A service alias keeps resolving through a rolling update

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-SD-ALIASES](#REQ-SWARM-SD-ALIASES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A service whose tasks have a network alias

A rolling update of the service that keeps the alias in the service's
`TaskTemplate.Networks` entry for its network, and in which at least one task keeps
running throughout, starts new tasks that also have that alias. Examples are an update in
start-first order and an update of fewer tasks at a time than are running. The alias does not
stop resolving for longer than the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION): queries for the alias sent more than that length apart, and every
query for the alias sent between them, do not all fail to resolve.

<a id="SWARM-SD-ALIAS-DROPPED-UPDATE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SD-ALIAS-DROPPED-UPDATE**: An alias that an update drops resolves until no task that has it runs

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-SD-ALIASES](#REQ-SWARM-SD-ALIASES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A service whose tasks have a network alias that no other service or container on
that network has

An update of the service removes the alias from its network attachment. While a task that has
the alias is one of the service's running tasks, the alias resolves on that network. Once none
of the service's running tasks has the alias, the alias does not resolve on that network. This
holds once the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) has
passed from the `die` event of the container of the last task that has the alias.

<a id="SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED**: A name on Swarm-scoped and local networks resolves to the Swarm address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED](#REQ-SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SD-WINDOWS-RESOLVER-PREFERENCE](#SWARM-SD-WINDOWS-RESOLVER-PREFERENCE)

*Applies to:* A container attached to a Swarm-scoped network and a local network, such as a
user-defined bridge network, and records for the same name on each of those networks
([Names and answers](container-dns.md#container-dns-names-and-answers) in [container-dns.md](container-dns.md))

A query from that container for the name gets the address on the Swarm-scoped network, and not
the address on the local network.

<a id="SWARM-SD-WINDOWS-RESOLVER-PREFERENCE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SD-WINDOWS-RESOLVER-PREFERENCE**: On Windows, a local network's record wins over the Swarm-scoped one

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-windows · *Platforms:* windows

*Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED](#SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED](#REQ-SWARM-SD-PREFER-SWARM-SCOPED)

Each network of a Windows container has its own embedded resolver, which answers
only from the records of its network. For a name that has records on a Swarm-scoped network and
on a local network, the resolver of the local network's adapter answers with the name's address
on the local network.

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL-NO-SERVICE**: On a node-local Swarm network, service names do not resolve

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](container-dns.md#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Rationale:* A node knows of other nodes' tasks only on networks that share records between nodes ([RAT-SWARM-NODE-LOCAL-NO-CLUSTER-RECORDS](swarm-networking.md#RAT-SWARM-NODE-LOCAL-NO-CLUSTER-RECORDS))

On that network, the embedded resolver handles a query for `<service>`,
`tasks.<service>` or a service alias as it handles a name that it does not have a

<a id="swarm-traffic-load-balancing-east-west-vip"></a>

## Load balancing (east-west VIP)

The client that sends to a VIP can be a service task or a standalone container on an `attachable`
overlay. Every expectation in this section holds for either client. The backends behind a VIP are
always service tasks. An expectation observed at the receiving end is observed from `task`. A VIP
load-balances across a set of tasks when flows to the VIP reach every task in the set. In this
section, a service's running tasks are those that [Service discovery](#swarm-traffic-service-discovery) defines.

<a id="SWARM-LB-PROTOCOLS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-LB-PROTOCOLS**: The VIP load-balances TCP, UDP and SCTP traffic

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-VIP-LOAD-BALANCING](#REQ-SWARM-VIP-LOAD-BALANCING) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPVS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPVS), [SWARM-HOST-IPVS-SCTP](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPVS-SCTP), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-SCTP](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-SCTP), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* After a load-balancer failure, failed backends get no flows until replaced ([SWARM-LBDIST-RECOVERY-INCOMPLETE](#SWARM-LBDIST-RECOVERY-INCOMPLETE)), In DSR mode, a task's connections to its own VIP reach only itself ([SWARM-LBHEALTH-DSR-OWN-VIP](#SWARM-LBHEALTH-DSR-OWN-VIP)), SCTP does not pass to or from containers on Windows nodes ([SWARM-SCALE-WINDOWS-SCTP](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-WINDOWS-SCTP))

The VIP load-balances TCP, UDP and SCTP flows across the service's running tasks.

<a id="SWARM-LB-NO-IPVS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-LB-NO-IPVS**: A node without IPVS logs that it cannot get ipvs family information

*Observed from:* log · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [SWARM-HOST-IPVS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPVS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes whose kernel does not offer IPVS, with the iptables backend, and a
service in vip mode with a running task on a network that is programmed on the node

The daemon log of that node contains `Could not get ipvs family information from the
kernel`.

<a id="SWARM-LB-FLOW-SAME-TASK"></a>

<a id="SWARM-LB-ROOTLESS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-LB-ROOTLESS**: In rootless mode with iptables, VIPs and published ports do not answer

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:mgr, task, client · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-INGPUB-EVERY-NODE](#SWARM-INGPUB-EVERY-NODE), [SWARM-LB-ANY-PORT](#SWARM-LB-ANY-PORT) · *Violates:* [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](../principles.md#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD), [REQ-SWARM-ROUTING-MESH](swarm-networking.md#REQ-SWARM-ROUTING-MESH), [REQ-SWARM-VIP-LOAD-BALANCING](#REQ-SWARM-VIP-LOAD-BALANCING)

*Applies to:* A daemon that runs in rootless mode with the iptables backend

`POST /swarm/init` responds 200, and `POST /networks/create` for an overlay
network responds 201 without a warning. A service in the `vip` endpoint mode on a user-defined
overlay network reports its tasks as running, but its VIP refuses connections. A service that
publishes a port through the routing mesh reports its task as running, but the port does not
answer. `POST /swarm/join` on another node, for a Swarm whose manager runs rootless,
responds with a 4xx or 5xx status, because the node's connection to the manager is refused.

<a id="swarm-traffic-distribution"></a>

### Distribution

The distribution property allows round-robin, equal-weight random, and 5-tuple hashing. It excludes
least-connections and other schedulers that depend on backend state. Clause (1), a limit, cannot
exclude them on its own because least-connections also converges to 1/*k* with identical backends.
Clause (2), invariance, tells them apart. The property does not fix a number of flows, and fixes no
tolerance on *fᵢ(n)/n* beyond the bound in clause (1). That bound allows for the nftables backend,
which splits a space of 65,536 equal buckets over the *k* tasks, so that each task gets ⌈65,536/*k*⌉ or ⌊65,536/*k*⌋ of them. A difference in connection holding time is one of the properties in
clause (2), and tells least-connections apart from round-robin.

> Let *H* be the set of running tasks, |*H*| = *k*, held constant. For *n* client flows let
> *fᵢ(n)* be the number of them that reach task *i*. Then (1) lim *fᵢ(n)/n* differs from 1/*k* by
> less than 1/65,536 for every *i* ∈ *H*, and (2) that limit is invariant to any observable
> property of the tasks: connection holding time, in-flight concurrency, latency, byte volume, or
> load.

*Applies to:* A Linux node with the iptables backend where a node-local failure to program a
load-balancer backend of a service occurred, and its cause has cleared

When a task is then added to the service, the node programs only that task's backend. A backend
whose programming failed does not get traffic through the node's load balancer until its task is
replaced. This includes every backend that arrived while the failure continued.

<a id="swarm-traffic-health-and-drain"></a>

### Health and drain

Every expectation in this subsection holds for flows through the service's VIP and for flows that
enter through an ingress-mode published port. A task shuts down gracefully when the orchestrator
shuts it down, for example after a scale-down, an update that replaces the task, the removal of its
service or a drain of its node. `POST /containers/{id}/stop` for the task's container is not
a graceful shutdown in these expectations. A flow starts on a node when its client is on that node,
or when it enters through a published port on that node. In these expectations, a task's process
ignores its stop signal and keeps accepting connections until it is killed at the end of the stop
grace period.

a local address. A connection from a task to the VIP of its own service reaches that task. The
other tasks of the service do not get these connections. The task gets them also while it does
not yet report healthy, and while it shuts down. Connections from other clients are
load-balanced.

<a id="swarm-traffic-published-ports"></a>

## Published ports

A published port is a port number and a protocol, as the `PublishedPort` and
`Protocol` of an entry in a service's `EndpointSpec.Ports` give them. An entry
without `Protocol` has the protocol `tcp`. Thus `53/tcp` and `53/udp` are two
different published ports. A published port is chosen when the request that creates or updates the
service sets its `PublishedPort` ([Port allocation](#swarm-traffic-port-allocation)).

A service publishes a port in one of two modes:

- `mode=ingress`, the default, publishes the port through the routing mesh on every node.
- `mode=host` publishes the port directly on the node that runs each task.

The expectations in this section hold for both modes. For a port that a service publishes in
`mode=host`, an expectation in this section that refers to a node's address, or to the
node's addresses, without saying which node, holds at the addresses of the nodes that run a task of
the service. They hold with `userland-proxy` true and with
`userland-proxy` false, unless an expectation names a value.
[Hairpin](#swarm-traffic-hairpin) covers hairpin paths. The [mode=ingress](#swarm-traffic-api-value-mode-ingress)
subsection covers what is specific to the routing mesh, and the
[mode=host](#swarm-traffic-api-value-mode-host) subsection covers what is specific to
`mode=host`.

Every expectation in this section and its subsections holds whether or not the `dsr` option
is set on the overlay networks that a service is attached to, other than the ingress network.

<a id="SWARM-PUB-V6-NO-USERLAND-PROXY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-PUB-V6-NO-USERLAND-PROXY**: Without userland-proxy, a client cannot reach a task over IPv6

*Observed from:* client, node · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING) · *Needs:* [BR-HOST-BR-NETFILTER-NO-PROXY](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-BR-NETFILTER-NO-PROXY), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A daemon with `userland-proxy` false, and a port published in ingress
mode, or in `mode=host` by a task whose gateway network is `docker_gwbridge`

A client cannot reach a task of the service through that port over IPv6, at any IPv6 address of
the node. This holds for TCP and UDP.

These IPv6 expectations do not mean that the service mesh supports IPv6. The service mesh is
IPv4-only ([*SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING*](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING)). The ingress network and the gateway network do not give
a task an IPv6 address. The proxy accepts traffic on `[::]` and forwards it to the task over IPv4,
as it does for any IPv4-only container. Thus the task sees the connection come from the proxy. For
this reason, the real-source expectation for `mode=host`,
[*SWARM-HOSTPUB-CLIENT-SOURCE*](#SWARM-HOSTPUB-CLIENT-SOURCE), does not hold for IPv6 clients.

For a port published in ingress mode, or in `mode=host` by a task whose gateway network
is `docker_gwbridge`, the userland proxy is necessary for the port to be reachable over
IPv6. Without the proxy, such a port is not reachable over IPv6
([*SWARM-PUB-V6-NO-USERLAND-PROXY*](#SWARM-PUB-V6-NO-USERLAND-PROXY)).

<a id="swarm-traffic-hairpin"></a>

### Hairpin

The six paths below are independent and can fail separately. The first five hold for both publish
modes. For `mode=host`, they hold on the nodes that run a task. In this subsection, the
node's addresses are its non-loopback IPv4 addresses, and each expectation holds at each of them, as
[README.md](README.md#readme-observed-from) says for the node's address. In this subsection, each task
or container that connects to the node's address must be attached to at least one network that is
not `internal`.

<a id="SWARM-HAIRPIN-USERLAND-PROXY"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-HAIRPIN-USERLAND-PROXY**: Hairpin reachability holds with userland-proxy true and false

*Observed from:* node, ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-PUB-HAIRPIN](#REQ-SWARM-PUB-HAIRPIN) · *Needs:* [BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* Auto-assignment gives an ingress port that a mode=host task holds ([SWARM-PUB-AUTO-ASSIGNED-PORT-HOST-MODE](#SWARM-PUB-AUTO-ASSIGNED-PORT-HOST-MODE)), A failure to publish one ingress port leaves the node publishing none ([SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE](#SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE))

Each other expectation of this subsection holds with `userland-proxy`
true and with `userland-proxy` false.

On Linux nodes, the two overlay expectations and the `mode=host` self-hairpin expectation
are the paths whose traffic leaves a bridge and then enters the same bridge again. An overlay
container reaches the node's address through `docker_gwbridge`. The connection then reaches
the ingress load balancer, or the task that serves the port, through `docker_gwbridge`
again. Only those paths are subject to the bridge's inter-container communication setting. A gateway
network that the daemon creates has inter-container communication disabled
([*SWARM-GWNET-NO-ICC*](#SWARM-GWNET-NO-ICC)).

The proxy can hide these paths ([*SWARM-HAIRPIN-USERLAND-PROXY*](#SWARM-HAIRPIN-USERLAND-PROXY)). For a `mode=host`
port, with the proxy, the connection ends in the host's network namespace and does not enter the
bridge again. Without the proxy, the traffic is DNATed back across the bridge. For a
`mode=ingress` port, the node DNATs IPv4 traffic that arrives on
`docker_gwbridge` back across the bridge with either `userland-proxy` value.
With `userland-proxy` true, the proxy then handles only IPv6 clients and the node's
connections to its loopback addresses.

<a id="swarm-traffic-api-value-mode-ingress"></a>

### `mode=ingress`

The routing mesh publishes an ingress-mode port on every node, whichever nodes run the service's
tasks.

<a id="swarm-traffic-port-allocation"></a>

#### Port allocation

An ingress-mode port is auto-assigned when the request that creates or updates the service does not
set its `PublishedPort`. `GET /services/{id}` then reports a published port for
it in `Endpoint.Ports`. The auto-assignment range is the set of published ports that an
auto-assigned port can get. A port of either publish mode is chosen when the request sets its
`PublishedPort`. A service's ports are allocated after the request responds. Where an
expectation in this subsection says that `GET /services/{id}` then reports a port, it
reports it within the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) after
the request responds.

<a id="SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535**: A published or target port above 65535 is accepted and never published

*Observed from:* api:mgr, client, node, ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-HOSTPUB-TARGET-OUT-OF-RANGE](#SWARM-HOSTPUB-TARGET-OUT-OF-RANGE), [SWARM-PORTALLOC-CHOSEN-OUT-OF-RANGE](#SWARM-PORTALLOC-CHOSEN-OUT-OF-RANGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-HOSTPUB-TARGET-OUT-OF-RANGE](#SWARM-HOSTPUB-TARGET-OUT-OF-RANGE), [SWARM-PORTALLOC-CHOSEN-OUT-OF-RANGE](#SWARM-PORTALLOC-CHOSEN-OUT-OF-RANGE) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST), [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS](swarm-networking.md#REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS)

`POST /services/create` with an ingress-mode `PublishedPort` above 65535
responds 201. `GET /services/{id}` then does not report the port in
`Endpoint.Ports`, and the service's tasks stay in the `new` state that
`GET /tasks` reports. With a `mode=host` `PublishedPort` above
65535, the request also responds 201, and each of the service's tasks is rejected with
`invalid port specification`. In `mode=host`, a `TargetPort`
above 65535 is also accepted. The service's tasks run, and `GET /tasks/{id}` reports no
port in `Status.PortStatus` for them. When such a port also sets
`PublishedPort`, a connection to that published port at the address of a node that
runs a task of the service does not reach the task.

<a id="SWARM-PORTALLOC-CONFLICT"></a>

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Applies to:* A leader manager that has checked a `POST /services/create` request, which
chooses a published port and protocol in either publish mode, for port conflicts, and has not
yet stored the request's service

published port and protocol, with at least one of the two requests choosing it in ingress mode,
for port conflicts before it stores the first request's service. Both requests respond 201.
`GET /services` then lists both services, each with that published port in
`Spec.EndpointSpec.Ports`.

On every node, `docker run -d -p` with the same port exits non-zero and prints the daemon's

with a healthcheck, first reports healthy.

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED), [SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START](#SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START), [SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-CLI](#SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-CLI), [SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-HTTP500](#SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-HTTP500) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-PORT-NO-CONFLICT](#REQ-SWARM-PORT-NO-CONFLICT)

<a id="SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-IN-USE-UNREACHABLE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-IN-USE-UNREACHABLE**: A service whose ingress ports a node failed to publish is unreachable there

*Observed from:* client · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE](#SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE](#SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE)

*Applies to:* A Linux node where a node-local failure to publish one of a service's ingress
ports occurred, because a process or container on the node uses the port or because the node
failed to program the firewall rules for the ports, and its cause still holds

Once no task from an earlier version of the service's spec remains, a client that connects to
the node's address on any of the service's published ports, in either IP version, does not reach
the service's tasks.

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-IN-USE-OLD-TASKS**: Adding an in-use port keeps earlier ports answering while old tasks run

*Observed from:* client · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-ROLLING-UPDATE](#REQ-SWARM-ROLLING-UPDATE) · *Needs:* [BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPVS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPVS), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* Other nodes send new flows to a task after it stops ([SWARM-CHURN-STOPPING-TASK-FLOWS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-STOPPING-TASK-FLOWS)), With firewalld, an ingress port does not answer at a node's IPv6 address ([SWARM-PUB-FIREWALLD-V6-INGRESS](#SWARM-PUB-FIREWALLD-V6-INGRESS))

*Applies to:* A node where a port is in use by a process or container, and a service that
publishes other ports in ingress mode

`POST /services/{id}/update` adds the port in use to the service in ingress mode. From
the response until `GET /tasks` first reports a `DesiredState` other than

[REQ-SWARM-PUB-IPV6-PROXY](#REQ-SWARM-PUB-IPV6-PROXY), [REQ-SWARM-ROUTING-MESH](swarm-networking.md#REQ-SWARM-ROUTING-MESH)

On a Linux node, a node-local failure to publish one of a service's ingress ports leaves the
node publishing none of them. The failure is a port that a process or container on the node uses
when the service is created or updated to publish it, or firewall rules for the ports that the
node fails to program. Once no task from an earlier version of the service's spec remains, a
client that connects to the node's address on any of the service's published ports, in either IP
version, does not reach the service's tasks. A process or container that uses one of the ports
keeps serving it. The daemon log reports the failure.

### `mode=host`

<a id="SWARM-HOSTPUB-TASK-NODES-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-HOSTPUB-TASK-NODES-ONLY**: A mode=host port is reachable only on nodes that run a task

A `mode=host` published port is reachable only at the addresses of nodes that run a
task of its service.

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-CLIENT-SOURCE](#REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-CLIENT-SOURCE) · *Needs:* [BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-HOSTPUB-CLIENT-SOURCE-V6**: With userland-proxy, a task does not see an IPv6 client's address

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-HOSTPUB-ASSIGNED-PORT-CTR**: The task's container reports the same assigned host port

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr (on the task's node) · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-PORT-REPORTED](#REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-PORT-REPORTED) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-HOSTPUB-ASSIGNED-PORT-CTR-CLI](#SWARM-HOSTPUB-ASSIGNED-PORT-CTR-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

task's container the host port that `GET /tasks/{id}` reports in
`Status.PortStatus`. No two entries of that `Ports` are identical. No list
of bindings in the `NetworkSettings.Ports` that `GET /containers/{id}/json`
reports for the container has two identical entries either.

<a id="SWARM-HOSTPUB-PLACEMENT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-HOSTPUB-PLACEMENT**: Tasks with the same chosen mode=host port never share a node

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-LOCAL](#REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-LOCAL) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Tasks that publish the same chosen `mode=host` port
([Port allocation](#swarm-traffic-port-allocation)) are never placed on the same node, whether they belong to
one service or several. `GET /tasks` never reports two such tasks with the same
`NodeID` and a `Status.State` from `assigned` to `running`, whatever
their `DesiredState`.

<a id="SWARM-HOSTPUB-PLACEMENT-PENDING"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-HOSTPUB-PLACEMENT-PENDING**: A task stays pending when every node already uses its mode=host port

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-LOCAL](#REQ-SWARM-HOSTPUB-LOCAL) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION)

*Applies to:* A Swarm in which each node runs a task that publishes a chosen
`mode=host` port ([Port allocation](#swarm-traffic-port-allocation))

A new task that publishes the same port in `mode=host` stays in the `pending` state
that `GET /tasks/{id}` reports in `Status.State`.

<a id="SWARM-HOSTPUB-TARGET-OUT-OF-RANGE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-HOSTPUB-TARGET-OUT-OF-RANGE**: A mode=host target port above 65535 runs tasks but reports no port

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pins:* [SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535](#SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535](#SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535)

`POST /services/create` for a service that publishes a `mode=host` port with
a `TargetPort` above 65535 responds 201. The service's tasks run, and `GET
/tasks/{id}` reports no port in `Status.PortStatus`.

<a id="swarm-traffic-egress-the-gateway-network"></a>

## Egress & the gateway network

<a id="SWARM-EGRESS-NON-INTERNAL"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-EGRESS-NON-INTERNAL**: A container on a non-internal overlay reaches the physical network

*Observed from:* task or ctr → underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS) · *Exact form:* [SWARM-CTR-DEFAULT-ROUTE](#SWARM-CTR-DEFAULT-ROUTE) · *Needs:* [BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

A container on a non-internal overlay has egress to the physical network.

<a id="SWARM-EGRESS-SOURCE-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-EGRESS-SOURCE-ADDRESS**: A container's egress traffic has the node's address as its source

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS) · *Needs:* [BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A container attached only to overlay networks, at least one of them not
`internal`

For the container's egress traffic, the source address that an underlay host observes is the
node's address, not the container's.

<a id="SWARM-EGRESS-INTERNAL-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-EGRESS-INTERNAL-ONLY**: A container on only internal overlays has no egress

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS](network-common.md#NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS)

A container attached only to `internal` overlays does not have egress.

<a id="SWARM-EGRESS-MIXED-INTERNAL"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-EGRESS-MIXED-INTERNAL**: A container on an internal and a non-internal overlay has egress

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS) · *Needs:* [BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NO-FORWARD-DROP), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A Windows container gets a default route from an internal overlay too ([SWARM-EGRESS-WINDOWS-MIXED-INTERNAL](#SWARM-EGRESS-WINDOWS-MIXED-INTERNAL))

A container on both an internal and a non-internal overlay has egress. Its default route is not
on the internal overlay.

<a id="SWARM-EGRESS-WINDOWS-MIXED-INTERNAL"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-EGRESS-WINDOWS-MIXED-INTERNAL**: A Windows container gets a default route from an internal overlay too

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-EGRESS-MIXED-INTERNAL](#SWARM-EGRESS-MIXED-INTERNAL) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS)

A Windows container attached to an `internal` overlay and to a non-internal overlay has a
default route through the gateway of each of the two networks.

<a id="SWARM-EGRESS-NO-NETWORK-DEFAULT-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-EGRESS-NO-NETWORK-DEFAULT-BRIDGE**: A task of a service with no network is on the default bridge only

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr (on the task's node) · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NO-NETWORK-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-NO-NETWORK-DEFAULT-BRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A Linux node that runs a task of a service whose spec names no network and that
publishes no port in ingress mode

On that node, `GET /containers/{id}/json` for the task's container reports the default
bridge network, `bridge`, and no other network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="swarm-traffic-gateway-network"></a>

### Gateway network

Each node has a gateway bridge network. Containers on the node's non-internal overlays reach the
physical network through it. This subsection holds on Linux nodes.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-AFTER-INIT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-AFTER-INIT**: A gateway bridge network exists within the ceiling after swarm init

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN)

Within the [*node leave and rejoin ceiling (120 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) after
`POST /swarm/init` responds 200 on a node, `GET /networks` on the node lists a
gateway bridge network.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-AFTER-JOIN"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-AFTER-JOIN**: A gateway bridge network exists within the ceiling after a join

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS](#SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with an ingress network

Within the [*node leave and rejoin ceiling (120 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) after
`POST /swarm/join` responds 200 on a node, `GET /networks` on that node lists a
gateway bridge network.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS**: A join without an ingress network does not create a gateway network

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-GWNET-AFTER-JOIN](#SWARM-GWNET-AFTER-JOIN), [SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS-FIRST-CTR](#SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS-FIRST-CTR) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE)

After `POST /swarm/join` responds 200 on a node, for a Swarm without an ingress network,
`GET /networks` on the node does not list a gateway bridge network until a container on
a non-internal overlay starts on the node.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS-FIRST-CTR"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS-FIRST-CTR**: Without ingress, the first overlay container adds a gateway network

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS](#SWARM-GWNET-NO-INGRESS)

*Applies to:* A node that joined a Swarm without an ingress network

Once a container on a non-internal overlay has started on the node, `GET /networks` on
the node lists a gateway bridge network.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-NAME**: A node's gateway bridge network is named docker_gwbridge

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

A node's gateway bridge network has the name `docker_gwbridge`.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-BRIDGE-IFACE-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-BRIDGE-IFACE-NAME**: The gateway network's bridge interface is named docker_gwbridge

*Observed from:* node · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

The bridge interface of a node's gateway bridge network has the name `docker_gwbridge`.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-OPERATOR-CREATED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-OPERATOR-CREATED**: An operator-created docker_gwbridge keeps its subnet and options

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A node where the operator created `docker_gwbridge` before its first
container on a non-internal overlay, and before it joined a Swarm with an ingress network, with
a subnet and with options of the `bridge` driver that the operator chose, including
options whose values differ from the ones the daemon sets on the gateway network it creates

After containers on non-internal overlays start on that node,
`GET /networks/docker_gwbridge` there reports the subnet and each option that the
operator gave it.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-OPERATOR-CREATED-ADDRESSES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-OPERATOR-CREATED-ADDRESSES**: Containers get addresses in an operator-created docker_gwbridge subnet

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE](#REQ-SWARM-GWBRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A node where the operator created `docker_gwbridge` before its first
container on a non-internal overlay, and before it joined a Swarm with an ingress network

The containers on non-internal overlays that then start on that node have gateway-network
addresses in the operator's subnet.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-NO-ICC"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-NO-ICC**: A daemon-created gateway network reports enable_icc as false

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ISOLATION](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ISOLATION) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A gateway network that the operator did not create

`GET /networks/{id}` for that network reports
`com.docker.network.bridge.enable_icc` as `false` in `Options`.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-NO-V6-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-NO-V6-ADDRESS**: A daemon-created gateway network gives containers no IPv6 address

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS](../principles.md#PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A gateway network that the operator did not create, and the containers on it,
among them a container on an overlay network created with `EnableIPv6` true

A container's interface on that network does not have an IPv6 address.

<a id="SWARM-GWNET-UNPUBLISHED-PORT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-GWNET-UNPUBLISHED-PORT**: An underlay host does not reach unpublished ports at a gateway address

*Observed from:* underlay → task or ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-UNPUBLISHED-NOT-EXPOSED](#REQ-SWARM-UNPUBLISHED-NOT-EXPOSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A container with an address on a node's gateway network, and an underlay host with
a route to that address via the node's underlay address

Traffic from that host to that address does not reach the container on a port that the container
does not publish.
